Case studiesServices Engineering practicesTechnologies Industries Company
Book a discovery call
On this page
Home›Industries›Consumer & wellness
Consumer & wellness

Consumer products people love, and trust with what matters most.

We build consumer health and wellness products where the honest data is the entire input: guidance drawn from a person's own history, privacy designed in at the moment data is written, and the engineering that turns a two-week motivation spike into a habit that lasts.

Book a discovery call
Guidance drawn from a person's own history rather than a template
Every record marked private or shared the moment it is written
Wearable data from whichever device somebody already owns

The constraint

In wellness the honest data is the entire input. People write things down in these products that they have not said out loud, and they only do that in a space they believe is private. So a privacy failure is not a breach with a remediation plan. It quietly turns every future entry into a performance, and the personalisation engine starts learning from a curated version of a person. The product does not break. It becomes a content library with a name in the header, which is the thing it existed to be better than.

Two of the consumer products we have built, chosen because each one turned on a constraint the category does not usually acknowledge.

Bonds, a relationship wellness app for two people

Two partners share one account, and each keeps a private space the other cannot see. That is the product. But a couple-level average over private answers is a lookup rather than an aggregate: know your own number and you know theirs. A design that is completely safe across a thousand users behaves differently across two, and it does not look different at review time, because it is the same design.

So privacy is classified when data is written rather than filtered when it is displayed, which means a screen that forgets to filter does not receive the records and hide them, it does not receive them. Couple-level figures show trend and direction rather than a number.

And AI context is scoped to the partner asking, so one partner cannot reach the other's private material by asking the coach about it. That closes the most obvious side channel in any product with a conversational interface over a shared dataset.

Read the full Bonds case study

A precision longevity platform

A leaked password is changed by the afternoon. There is no equivalent action available for a genome, at any price, for the rest of somebody's life. It is also not only theirs, because it discloses a great deal about parents, siblings and children who never consented to anything. And it identifies by itself, so anonymisation in the ordinary sense is not available.

That changes the question from how to recover from a breach to how to be worth less to somebody who achieves one. The biological data and the identity it belongs to are held apart, encrypted under keys managed separately from the data they protect, and the raw marker set is read by the interpretation step and almost nothing else. Everything downstream reads a report.

The wearable side is a clock problem. Four data types on three different clocks, where genetics never changes, a blood panel is true around a date, and a watch changes every few seconds, and treating them as three points on one timeline produces a confident statement about a person that none of the inputs support.

Read the full case study

These are two of the consumer platforms we have worked on. The full set is in our case studies, including work we cannot name.

What we would expect to deal with on your product

Not a service list. Four problems that show up on most consumer wellness products, and the decision we made when each showed up on ours.

Personalisation that runs at question time puts a multi-second wait in front of the smallest, most frequent interactions, exactly the ones a daily habit depends on, and it gets slower and more expensive in direct proportion to how well the product is doing. So the work happens ahead of need and the morning open is a database read rather than an inference.

Sending a user's full history to a model with every question fails on three counts at once. Cost and latency scale with tenure, so the most engaged users get the worst experience. Answer quality degrades as the relevant signal is buried in months of routine entries. And far more intimate material leaves the platform than any single question justifies. A compact derived profile, rebuilt in the background, is the same input at a fixed size.

A model given a description of a frightening situation will produce fluent, specific, plausible advice, and a person with nobody else to ask at two in the morning will act on it. There is no error state for a well written response to the wrong kind of message, so the decision about what kind of message this is has to be made before generation rather than reviewed after it.

A notification is granted once and revoked permanently. Too few and the habit does not form, which is recoverable. Too many and the user turns them off at the operating system level, which is close to unrecoverable, because the product cannot ask again through the channel it just lost.

Privacy, and what it actually costs to get right

In this category privacy is not a risk control sitting beside the product. It is the input. Honest data is the only data worth personalising from, and people are only honest in a space they trust, so the privacy design and the product quality are the same thing.

Classification at write rather than filtering at read, so a feature nobody has written yet inherits the boundary by default rather than being audited into compliance.

Enforcement below the application, so a screen that forgets to filter does not receive the records at all.

AI context scoped to the person asking, which closes the side channel a conversational interface opens over a shared dataset.

Notifications that carry a pointer rather than content, because a lock screen is the least controllable surface in a mobile product, and in a shared-account product the person most likely to be looking at it is the one who must not.

Statistics over private inputs constrained so an individual value cannot be reconstructed from them.

The most sensitive material travelling the shortest distance it can, and leaving without a name attached.

We build to the relevant data protection standards, and we don't claim certifications we don't hold. That restraint is a credential in a category where the data is this personal.

Retention, and why it is an engineering problem here

Wellness products drop off steeply after the first fortnight. Motivation carries two weeks. After that only habit does, and most products have nothing in place for the handover.

So the daily ask is sized for the worst week rather than the best one. An exercise that needs a good evening only happens on good evenings, and the weeks that matter most are rarely the good ones.

Reinforcement sits on consistency rather than volume, and accumulated progress is made visible, because it is the one motivator that strengthens over time while every other one decays.

And a streak that occasionally eats a day is worse than no streak, because it teaches people the number is not real. That is a concurrency problem before it is a product one, and it is why shared state is written through a single path rather than from two devices at once.

Which trust services criteria this work is judged on

Privacy, which is the criterion this category lives on. It concerns the people the data is about and what say they have over it, and in a shared-account product it includes the boundary between two people inside one account.

Processing integrity, which is the one nobody expects in a consumer app. It asks whether the system does what it claims, completely and accurately, and a shared counter that silently loses a day fails that test. Here it is not a cosmetic bug, because the counter is the reinforcement mechanism.

Confidentiality, in the separation between what is shared and what is private inside a single account.

The boundary, stated plainly. The control set is designed against the criteria rather than mapped to them afterwards. That is a statement about how a platform was built, not a claim to hold an attestation, and where a client needs one, the work is theirs to complete with an auditor. We don't claim certifications we don't hold.

What the platforms actually do

Not by sending a person's history to a model with every question. In event-driven systems, unhandled backpressure and non-idempotent processing are how data quietly goes missing or corrupt. We build resilient Go systems on Kafka, Pub/Sub, and Kinesis that assume failure will happen, retry strategies, dead-letter queues, end-to-end observability, so the pipelines behind your critical workflows stay trustworthy.

How we help

We map event contracts up front, make processing idempotent, and design retries, DLQs, and back-pressure deliberately rather than discovering them in production.

Networking performance usually dies in the details, connection handling, buffer management, TLS handshakes. How we help

We profile the hot paths, tune connection and buffer handling, and verify tail latency against realistic load so gains hold in production.

We build streaming and batch pipelines tuned for throughput, version transformations, and add observability so data flows stay reliable.

We build Spring Boot applications that drop into the architecture and data models you already run, rather than fighting them. Backend reliability, clean service boundaries, and systems that scale without a rewrite are what we optimise for, so delivery stays quick and the platform keeps extending confidently as the roadmap moves.

Enterprise Web Application Development

A monolith slows delivery and hems in how independently teams can work. We build Spring Boot web applications on Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux that hold complex business logic, connect to legacy systems, and scale out horizontally as traffic climbs. Layered architecture keeps concerns separate, Spring Data handles persistence, and REST APIs feed the frontend, so features ship faster and the code stays good through years of iteration.

Breaking a core monolith into microservices changes how the whole platform behaves. We design distributed systems on Spring Boot and Spring Cloud with service discovery, resiliency, and centralised configuration handled properly. The services run in Kubernetes-orchestrated containers, talk over synchronous APIs or messaging, and use proven patterns to keep data consistent across boundaries, so you can scale services independently and deploy without taking the whole system down.

How we help

We apply Spring Cloud patterns for discovery, config, and resilience, and define data-consistency and deployment boundaries so services scale independently.

An API has to stay stable even as the system behind it keeps changing. We build APIs with Spring Boot, usually RESTful, with asynchronous and event-driven patterns where they suit the job, handling authentication through Spring Security, rate-limiting to protect resources, and returning clear errors. Partners and internal teams get integration points they can depend on rather than ones that break on every release.

How we help

We version the API contract, secure it with Spring Security, and add rate limiting and clear error responses so integrations stay stable across releases.

Older Spring applications tend to accumulate configuration sprawl and security debt. We migrate them to Spring Boot. XML configuration swapped for annotations, deprecated dependencies updated, the whole thing refactored onto auto-configuration. Parallel test environments, incremental rollouts, and documentation of the architectural calls keep the move safe, leaving you modern infrastructure that's easier to maintain, monitor, and extend.

How we help

We swap XML for annotation-based config, update deprecated dependencies, and roll out incrementally with parallel test environments so migration remains safe.

Get authentication or authorisation wrong and you've bought yourself compliance risk and a breach waiting to happen. We implement Spring Security that ties into OAuth2 providers, enforces role-based access, and guards endpoints with method-level annotations with JWT handling, session security, CSRF protection, and audit trails all in place. Your applications clear their security requirements without dragging users through clunky login flows.

How we help

We integrate OAuth2 providers, enforce role-based and method-level access, and manage JWT, session security, and CSRF while keeping auth flows smooth.

Data access layers bloat with boilerplate and quietly sprout N+1 query problems. We build ours on Spring Data JPA and Spring Data JDBC, persistence abstracted, queries tuned, transactions handled consistently with support for multiple databases where needed, caching via Redis or Hazelcast, and migrations run through Flyway or Liquibase. Teams ship features without rebuilding the data layer, and you keep fine-grained control over queries and indexes.

How we help

We abstract persistence with Spring Data, resolve N+1 and slow queries, and version migrations with Flyway or Liquibase while retaining control over indexes.

Traditional deployments can't touch the elasticity the cloud offers. We build cloud-native Spring Boot applications on AWS, Azure, or GCP that lean on managed services for databases, messaging, and caching, apply Spring Cloud service-mesh patterns, externalise configuration to cut down on container rebuilds, and instrument with distributed tracing, so the application scales with demand on its own and fits cleanly into cloud-native tooling.

How we help

We externalise configuration, lean on managed cloud services, and instrument with distributed tracing so apps scale automatically and stay observable.

lcp-discovery-insight.title: LCP request discovery
lcp-discovery-insight.description: [Optimize LCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/lcp-discovery) by making the LCP image discoverable from the HTML immediately, and avoiding lazy-loading

final-screenshot.title: Final Screenshot
final-screenshot.description: The last screenshot captured of the pageload.

max-potential-fid.title: Max Potential First Input Delay
max-potential-fid.description: The maximum potential First Input Delay that your users could experience is the duration of the longest task. [Learn more about the Maximum Potential First Input Delay metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-max-potential-fid/).

network-requests.title: Network Requests
network-requests.description: Lists the network requests that were made during page load.

long-tasks.title: Avoid long main-thread tasks
long-tasks.description: Lists the longest tasks on the main thread, useful for identifying worst contributors to input delay. [Learn how to avoid long main-thread tasks](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-long-tasks)

document-latency-insight.title: Document request latency
document-latency-insight.description: Your first network request is the most important. [Reduce its latency](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/document-latency) by avoiding redirects, ensuring a fast server response, and enabling text compression.

server-response-time.title: Initial server response time was short
server-response-time.description: Keep the server response time for the main document short because all other requests depend on it. [Learn more about the Time to First Byte metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/time-to-first-byte/).

total-byte-weight.title: Avoids enormous network payloads
total-byte-weight.description: Large network payloads cost users real money and are highly correlated with long load times. [Learn how to reduce payload sizes](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/total-byte-weight/).

largest-contentful-paint.title: Largest Contentful Paint
largest-contentful-paint.description: Largest Contentful Paint marks the time at which the largest text or image is painted. [Learn more about the Largest Contentful Paint metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-largest-contentful-paint/)

redirects.title: Avoid multiple page redirects
redirects.description: Redirects introduce additional delays before the page can be loaded. [Learn how to avoid page redirects](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/redirects/).

total-blocking-time.title: Total Blocking Time
total-blocking-time.description: Sum of all time periods between FCP and Time to Interactive, when task length exceeded 50ms, expressed in milliseconds. [Learn more about the Total Blocking Time metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-total-blocking-time/).

network-server-latency.title: Server Backend Latencies
network-server-latency.description: Server latencies can impact web performance. If the server latency of an origin is high, it's an indication the server is overloaded or has poor backend performance. [Learn more about server response time](https://hpbn.co/primer-on-web-performance/#analyzing-the-resource-waterfall).

speed-index.title: Speed Index
speed-index.description: Speed Index shows how quickly the contents of a page are visibly populated. [Learn more about the Speed Index metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/speed-index/).

cache-insight.title: Use efficient cache lifetimes
cache-insight.description: A long cache lifetime can speed up repeat visits to your page. [Learn more about caching](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/cache).

unused-css-rules.title: Reduce unused CSS
unused-css-rules.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused CSS](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-css-rules/).

viewport-insight.title: Optimize viewport for mobile
viewport-insight.description: Tap interactions may be [delayed by up to 300 ms](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/viewport) if the viewport is not optimized for mobile.

non-composited-animations.title: Avoid non-composited animations
non-composited-animations.description: Animations which are not composited can be janky and increase CLS. [Learn how to avoid non-composited animations](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/non-composited-animations/)

lcp-breakdown-insight.title: LCP breakdown
lcp-breakdown-insight.description: Each [subpart has specific improvement strategies](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/lcp-breakdown). Ideally, most of the LCP time should be spent on loading the resources, not within delays.

user-timings.title: User Timing marks and measures
user-timings.description: Consider instrumenting your app with the User Timing API to measure your app's real-world performance during key user experiences. [Learn more about User Timing marks](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/user-timings/).

inp-breakdown-insight.title: INP breakdown
inp-breakdown-insight.description: Start investigating [how to improve INP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/inp-breakdown) by looking at the longest subpart.

unminified-javascript.title: Minify JavaScript
unminified-javascript.description: Minifying JavaScript files can reduce payload sizes and script parse time. [Learn how to minify JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unminified-javascript/).

forced-reflow-insight.title: Forced reflow
forced-reflow-insight.description: A forced reflow occurs when JavaScript queries geometric properties (such as `offsetWidth`) after styles have been invalidated by a change to the DOM state. This can result in poor performance. Learn more about [forced reflows](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/forced-reflow) and possible mitigations.

cumulative-layout-shift.title: Cumulative Layout Shift
cumulative-layout-shift.description: Cumulative Layout Shift measures the movement of visible elements within the viewport. [Learn more about the Cumulative Layout Shift metric](https://web.dev/articles/cls).

duplicated-javascript-insight.title: Duplicated JavaScript
duplicated-javascript-insight.description: Remove large, [duplicate JavaScript modules](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/duplicated-javascript) from bundles to reduce unnecessary bytes consumed by network activity.

legacy-javascript-insight.title: Legacy JavaScript
legacy-javascript-insight.description: Polyfills and transforms enable older browsers to use new JavaScript features. However, many aren't necessary for modern browsers. Consider modifying your JavaScript build process to not transpile [Baseline](https://web.dev/articles/baseline-and-polyfills) features, unless you know you must support older browsers. [Learn why most sites can deploy ES6+ code without transpiling](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/legacy-javascript)

layout-shifts.title: Avoid large layout shifts
layout-shifts.description: These are the largest layout shifts observed on the page. Each table item represents a single layout shift, and shows the element that shifted the most. Below each item are possible root causes that led to the layout shift. Some of these layout shifts may not be included in the CLS metric value due to [windowing](https://web.dev/articles/cls#what_is_cls). [Learn how to improve CLS](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-cls)

unused-javascript.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
unused-javascript.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-javascript/).

first-contentful-paint.title: First Contentful Paint
first-contentful-paint.description: First Contentful Paint marks the time at which the first text or image is painted. [Learn more about the First Contentful Paint metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/first-contentful-paint/).

image-delivery-insight.title: Improve image delivery
image-delivery-insight.description: Reducing the download time of images can improve the perceived load time of the page and LCP. [Learn more about optimizing image size](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/image-delivery)

interactive.title: Time to Interactive
interactive.description: Time to Interactive is the amount of time it takes for the page to become fully interactive. [Learn more about the Time to Interactive metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/interactive/).

a11y-color-contrast.title: Contrast
a11y-color-contrast.description: These are opportunities to improve the legibility of your content.

seo-crawl.title: Crawling and Indexing
seo-crawl.description: To appear in search results, crawlers need access to your app.

a11y-tables-lists.title: Tables and lists
a11y-tables-lists.description: These are opportunities to improve the experience of reading tabular or list data using assistive technology, like a screen reader.

a11y-best-practices.title: Best practices
a11y-best-practices.description: These items highlight common accessibility best practices.

agent-accessibility.title: Agent Accessibility
agent-accessibility.description: These audits highlight best practices for improving the accessibility of the website for AI agents.

a11y-names-labels.title: Names and labels
a11y-names-labels.description: These are opportunities to improve the semantics of the controls in your application. This may enhance the experience for users of assistive technology, like a screen reader.

a11y-language.title: Internationalization and localization
a11y-language.description: These are opportunities to improve the interpretation of your content by users in different locales.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: More information about the performance of your application. These numbers don't [directly affect](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring/) the Performance score.

a11y-aria.title: ARIA
a11y-aria.description: These are opportunities to improve the usage of ARIA in your application which may enhance the experience for users of assistive technology, like a screen reader.

insights.title: Insights
insights.description: These insights are also available in the Chrome DevTools Performance Panel - [record a trace](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/reference) to view more detailed information.

a11y-audio-video.title: Audio and video
a11y-audio-video.description: These are opportunities to provide alternative content for audio and video. This may improve the experience for users with hearing or vision impairments.

seo-mobile.title: Mobile Friendly
seo-mobile.description: Make sure your pages are mobile friendly so users don’t have to pinch or zoom in order to read the content pages. [Learn how to make pages mobile-friendly](https://developers.google.com/search/mobile-sites/).

a11y-navigation.title: Navigation
a11y-navigation.description: These are opportunities to improve keyboard navigation in your application.

seo-content.title: Content Best Practices
seo-content.description: Format your HTML in a way that enables crawlers to better understand your app’s content.

[Learn more about server response time](https://hpbn.co/primer-on-web-performance/#analyzing-the-resource-waterfall).

mainthread-work-breakdown.title: Minimize main-thread work
mainthread-work-breakdown.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. [Learn how to minimize main-thread work](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/mainthread-work-breakdown/)

final-screenshot.title: Final Screenshot
final-screenshot.description: The last screenshot captured of the pageload.

resource-summary.title: Resources Summary
resource-summary.description: Aggregates all network requests and groups them by type

unused-javascript.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
unused-javascript.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-javascript/).

lcp-breakdown-insight.title: LCP breakdown
lcp-breakdown-insight.description: Each [subpart has specific improvement strategies](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/lcp-breakdown). Ideally, most of the LCP time should be spent on loading the resources, not within delays.

items.nodeLabel: Whether you're shaping a first product or scaling an established platform, we d…

duplicated-javascript-insight.title: Duplicated JavaScript
duplicated-javascript-insight.description: Remove large, [duplicate JavaScript modules](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/duplicated-javascript) from bundles to reduce unnecessary bytes consumed by network activity.

unused-css-rules.title: Reduce unused CSS
unused-css-rules.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused CSS](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-css-rules/).

user-timings.title: User Timing marks and measures
user-timings.description: Consider instrumenting your app with the User Timing API to measure your app's real-world performance during key user experiences. [Learn more about User Timing marks](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/user-timings/).

main-thread-tasks.title: Tasks
main-thread-tasks.description: Lists the toplevel main thread tasks that executed during page load.

lcp-discovery-insight.title: LCP request discovery
lcp-discovery-insight.description: [Optimize LCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/lcp-discovery) by making the LCP image discoverable from the HTML immediately, and avoiding lazy-loading

inp-breakdown-insight.title: INP breakdown
inp-breakdown-insight.description: Start investigating [how to improve INP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/inp-breakdown) by looking at the longest subpart.

cache-insight.title: Use efficient cache lifetimes
cache-insight.description: A long cache lifetime can speed up repeat visits to your page. [Learn more about caching](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/cache).

network-dependency-tree-insight.title: Network dependency tree
network-dependency-tree-insight.description: [Avoid chaining critical requests](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/network-dependency-tree) by reducing the length of chains, reducing the download size of resources, or deferring the download of unnecessary resources to improve page load.

items.title: Preconnected origins
items.description: [preconnect](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/uses-rel-preconnect/) hints help the browser establish a connection earlier in the page load, saving time when the first request for that origin is made. The following are the origins that the page preconnected to.

items.title: Preconnect candidates

value.value: No additional origins are good candidates for preconnecting

items.description: Add [preconnect](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/uses-rel-preconnect/) hints to your most important origins, but try to use no more than 4.

long-tasks.title: Avoid long main-thread tasks
long-tasks.description: Lists the longest tasks on the main thread, useful for identifying worst contributors to input delay. [Learn how to avoid long main-thread tasks](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-long-tasks)

forced-reflow-insight.title: Forced reflow
forced-reflow-insight.description: A forced reflow occurs when JavaScript queries geometric properties (such as `offsetWidth`) after styles have been invalidated by a change to the DOM state. This can result in poor performance. Learn more about [forced reflows](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/forced-reflow) and possible mitigations.

layout-shifts.title: Avoid large layout shifts
layout-shifts.description: These are the largest layout shifts observed on the page. Each table item represents a single layout shift, and shows the element that shifted the most. Below each item are possible root causes that led to the layout shift. Some of these layout shifts may not be included in the CLS metric value due to [windowing](https://web.dev/articles/cls#what_is_cls). [Learn how to improve CLS](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-cls)

unminified-javascript.title: Minify JavaScript
unminified-javascript.description: Minifying JavaScript files can reduce payload sizes and script parse time. [Learn how to minify JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unminified-javascript/).

font-display-insight.title: Font display
font-display-insight.description: Consider setting [`font-display`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/font-display) to `swap` or `optional` to ensure text is consistently visible. `swap` can be further optimized to mitigate layout shifts with [font metric overrides](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/font-fallbacks).

viewport-insight.title: Optimize viewport for mobile
viewport-insight.description: Tap interactions may be [delayed by up to 300 ms](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/viewport) if the viewport is not optimized for mobile.

cumulative-layout-shift.title: Cumulative Layout Shift
cumulative-layout-shift.description: Cumulative Layout Shift measures the movement of visible elements within the viewport. [Learn more about the Cumulative Layout Shift metric](https://web.dev/articles/cls).

non-composited-animations.title: Avoid non-composited animations
non-composited-animations.description: Animations which are not composited can be janky and increase CLS. [Learn how to avoid non-composited animations](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/non-composited-animations/)

third-parties-insight.title: 3rd parties
third-parties-insight.description: 3rd party code can significantly impact load performance. [Reduce and defer loading of 3rd party code](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/third-parties) to prioritize your page's content.

interactive.title: Time to Interactive
interactive.description: Time to Interactive is the amount of time it takes for the page to become fully interactive. [Learn more about the Time to Interactive metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/interactive/).

cls-culprits-insight.title: Layout shift culprits
cls-culprits-insight.description: Layout shifts occur when elements move absent any user interaction. [Investigate the causes of layout shifts](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/cls-culprit), such as elements being added, removed, or their fonts changing as the page loads.

total-byte-weight.title: Avoids enormous network payloads
total-byte-weight.description: Large network payloads cost users real money and are highly correlated with long load times. [Learn how to reduce payload sizes](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/total-byte-weight/).

image-delivery-insight.title: Improve image delivery
image-delivery-insight.description: Reducing the download time of images can improve the perceived load time of the page and LCP. [Learn more about optimizing image size](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/image-delivery)

items.reason: This image file is larger than it needs to be (412x132) for its displayed dimensions (197x63). Use responsive images to reduce the image download size.

network-rtt.title: Network Round Trip Times
network-rtt.description: Network round trip times (RTT) have a large impact on performance. If the RTT to an origin is high, it's an indication that servers closer to the user could improve performance. [Learn more about the Round Trip Time](https://hpbn.co/primer-on-latency-and-bandwidth/).

max-potential-fid.title: Max Potential First Input Delay
max-potential-fid.description: The maximum potential First Input Delay that your users could experience is the duration of the longest task. [Learn more about the Maximum Potential First Input Delay metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-max-potential-fid/).

largest-contentful-paint.title: Largest Contentful Paint
largest-contentful-paint.description: Largest Contentful Paint marks the time at which the largest text or image is painted. [Learn more about the Largest Contentful Paint metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-largest-contentful-paint/)

render-blocking-insight.title: Render-blocking requests
render-blocking-insight.description: Requests are blocking the page's initial render, which may delay LCP. [Deferring or inlining](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/render-blocking) can move these network requests out of the critical path.

legacy-javascript-insight.title: Legacy JavaScript
legacy-javascript-insight.description: Polyfills and transforms enable older browsers to use new JavaScript features. However, many aren't necessary for modern browsers. Consider modifying your JavaScript build process to not transpile [Baseline](https://web.dev/articles/baseline-and-polyfills) features, unless you know you must support older browsers. [Learn why most sites can deploy ES6+ code without transpiling](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/performance/insights/legacy-javascript)

screenshot-thumbnails.title: Screenshot Thumbnails
screenshot-thumbnails.description: This is what the load of your site looked like.

bootup-time.title: JavaScript execution time
bootup-time.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. [Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/bootup-time/).

server-response-time.title: Initial server response time was short
server-response-time.description: Keep the server response time for the main document short because all other requests depend on it. [Learn more about the Time to First Byte metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/time-to-first-byte/).

speed-index.title: Speed Index
speed-index.description: Speed Index shows how quickly the contents of a page are visibly populated. [Learn more about the Speed Index metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/speed-index/).

total-blocking-time.title: Total Blocking Time
total-blocking-time.description: Sum of all time periods between FCP and Time to Interactive, when task length exceeded 50ms, expressed in milliseconds. [Learn more about the Total Blocking Time metric](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/lighthouse-total-blocking-time/).

seo-crawl.title: Crawling and Indexing
seo-crawl.description: To appear in search results, crawlers need access to your app.

seo-content.title: Content Best Practices
seo-content.description: Format your HTML in a way that enables crawlers to better understand your app’s content.

insights.title: Insights
insights.description: These insights are also available in the Chrome DevTools Performance Panel - [record a trace](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/reference) to view more detailed information.

a11y-best-practices.title: Best practices
a11y-best-practices.description: These items highlight common accessibility best practices.

a11y-language.title: Internationalization and localization
a11y-language.description: These are opportunities to improve the interpretation of your content by users in different locales.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: More information about the performance of your application. These numbers don't [directly affect](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring/) the Performance score.

a11y-audio-video.title: Audio and video
a11y-audio-video.description: These are opportunities to provide alternative content for audio and video. This may improve the experience for users with hearing or vision impairments.

a11y-navigation.title: Navigation
a11y-navigation.description: These are opportunities to improve keyboard navigation in your application.

a11y-aria.title: ARIA
a11y-aria.description: These are opportunities to improve the usage of ARIA in your application which may enhance the experience for users of assistive technology, like a screen reader.

a11y-color-contrast.title: Contrast
a11y-color-contrast.description: These are opportunities to improve the legibility of your content.

seo-mobile.title: Mobile Friendly
seo-mobile.description: Make sure your pages are mobile friendly so users don’t have to pinch or zoom in order to read the content pages. [Learn how to make pages mobile-friendly](https://developers.google.com/search/mobile-sites/).

a11y-names-labels.title: Names and labels
a11y-names-labels.description: These are opportunities to improve the semantics of the controls in your application. This may enhance the experience for users of assistive technology, like a screen reader.

a11y-tables-lists.title: Tables and lists
a11y-tables-lists.description: These are opportunities to improve the experience of reading tabular or list data using assistive technology, like a screen reader.

agent-accessibility.title: Agent Accessibility
agent-accessibility.description: These audits highlight best practices for improving the accessibility of the website for AI agents.
